description: SQL/backend: fix the critical turn-rotation bug (last player skipped per round in FFA, same risk in team mode) and add the admin backend. ROOT CAUSE: fn_advance_turn (FFA) advances with `turn_order > v_cur_order order by turn_order asc limit 1` plus wrap-around, which assumes turn_order is a unique contiguous 0..n-1 sequence. join_room sets turn_order = current player count, so after any lobby leave/kick a later joiner gets a DUPLICATE turn_order; with a duplicate at the top value the `>` comparison can never select the second holder, so one player (typically the highest turn_order, the 'last' player) is skipped every round. Fix advancement to be independent of gaps/duplicates by ordering alive players deterministically on the tuple (turn_order, id) and picking the next tuple strictly greater than the current player's (turn_order, id), wrapping to the first. Apply the analogous (turn_order, id) tuple fix to team-mode team advancement. Leave fn_pick_first_subject's `order by random()` opener untouched (must stay random). Independent of FEAT-002/003 except that FEAT-002 calls the new RPC and relies on is_admin.
steps: In supabase/functions.sql, rewrite the FFA branch of fn_advance_turn so it does NOT depend on contiguous/unique turn_order. Read the current player's (turn_order, id) via `select turn_order, id into v_cur_order, v_cur_id from public.players where id = v_round.active_subject_id;`. Then select the next alive player with `where room_id = v_room.id and is_alive and (turn_order, id) > (v_cur_order, v_cur_id) order by turn_order asc, id asc limit 1`; if null, wrap with `where room_id = v_room.id and is_alive order by turn_order asc, id asc limit 1`. Declare v_cur_id uuid alongside v_cur_order.

In the team branch of fn_advance_turn, apply the same tuple ordering for robustness: read the current team's (turn_order, id), then find the next team with alive members using `(t.turn_order, t.id) > (v_cur_team_order, v_cur_team_id)` ordered by `t.turn_order asc, t.id asc`, wrapping to the first team with alive members the same way. Keep the alive-members EXISTS filter and keep member selection `order by random()`. Declare the needed local vars.

Add a written verification block as a SQL COMMENT at the end of fn_advance_turn (or just above it) proving full coverage: e.g. a commented simulation note stating that for N alive players with any turn_order values (including duplicates/gaps), starting from any opener the (turn_order,id) successor relation plus wrap forms a single cycle visiting every alive player exactly once per round. Also note the opener stays random via fn_pick_first_subject.

In supabase/functions.sql, modify join_room: add a new boolean parameter `p_is_admin boolean default false` to the signature (and the matching `drop function if exists public.join_room(text, text, text, text);` already present — add a drop for the OLD 4-arg signature so the new 5-arg replaces cleanly). On insert into public.players, set `is_admin` from p_is_admin. In the existing-device early-return path, also keep is_admin as-is (do not downgrade). Keep ROOM_FULL at >= 16.

In supabase/functions.sql, modify kick_player: after the NOT_HOST / NOT_LOBBY / CANT_KICK_HOST checks, add `if exists (select 1 from public.players where id = p_target_player and room_id = p_room_id and is_admin) then raise exception 'CANT_KICK_ADMIN'; end if;` before the delete.

Create supabase/migration-v9.sql (NEW FILE, do not edit v2..v8). Add `alter table public.players add column if not exists is_admin boolean not null default false;`. Then create a PIN-gated RPC `list_active_rooms(p_pin text)` following the migration-v7 list_suggestions pattern: SECURITY DEFINER, `if p_pin is distinct from public.fn_admin_pin() then raise exception 'BAD_PIN'; end if;`, returning table (code text, status text, player_count int, created_at timestamptz) selecting from public.rooms with a correlated player count, ordered by created_at desc. Grant execute to anon, authenticated. Include a header comment matching the style of other migrations and a note to re-run functions.sql after.

Confirm every new/changed RPC in functions.sql remains covered by the file-wide `grant execute on all functions in schema public to anon, authenticated;` at the end (join_room and kick_player are; list_active_rooms is granted explicitly in migration-v9).
acceptance_criteria: fn_advance_turn FFA branch selects the next alive player using the (turn_order, id) tuple with wrap-around and no longer assumes unique/contiguous turn_order.
fn_advance_turn team branch uses (turn_order, id) tuple ordering for team advancement and still picks a random alive member.
fn_pick_first_subject is unchanged and still uses order by random() for the opener.
join_room accepts p_is_admin and persists players.is_admin; kick_player raises CANT_KICK_ADMIN for admin targets.
supabase/migration-v9.sql exists, adds players.is_admin, and defines + grants list_active_rooms(p_pin) following the list_suggestions PIN pattern.
A written simulation/reasoning note in SQL comments shows every alive player gets exactly one turn per round regardless of turn_order duplicates/gaps.
